newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Politics, economic reform change face of N.Zealand.
newsitem.headline: Politics, economic reform change face of N.Zealand.

text.p: These are the key facts about New Zealand, which is due to hold a general election on Saturday.

AREA - 268,112 sq km (99,166 sq miles) comprising the North and South Islands and a number of smaller islands. New Zealand is 1,600 km (1,000 miles) east of Australia and roughly similar in size to Britain or Japan.
POPULATION - New Zealand has a population of 3.66 million, of whom about 13 percent are Maori and the rest mainly of European descent.
CONSTITUTION - New Zealand, a Commonwealth member, is a constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy. Queen Elizabeth II is head of state, while the prime minister is the head of government.
Saturday's election is the first under a German-style system of proportional representation which favours minority or coalition governments. This replaces British-style first-past-the-post.

The single-chamber House of Representatives will be expanded to at least 120 members from the previous 99. Parliament is under the largely symbolic authority of the Queen, represented in New Zealand by an appointed governor-general who may act as a facilitator in negotiations to form a coalition.
LANGUAGE - English and Maori are the official languages.

ECONOMY - Per capita gross domestic product (GDP) in the March year was NZ$24,434 (US$16,786). Real GDP grew by 2.6 percent in the year to June and is forecast by Treasury to grow by an annual three to four percent in the next three years.
Underlying inflation was 2.3 percent in the June 1996 year -- outside the zero to two percent target band in which the central Reserve Bank of New Zealand is mandated to keep it.

The last three governments have vigorously pursued free market policies and virtually removed all subsidies, transforming New Zealand from one of the western world's most regulated and protected economies into one of its most open and competitive.

New Zealand relies on primary product exports, especially meat, wool and dairy products. Total merchandise exports in the year to August were NZ$20.91 billion (US$14.4 billion), while imports totalled NZ$21.6 billion (US$14.9 billion)

Australia, the European Union, Asia and the United States account for the majority of New Zealand's overseas trade, but important links have been developed with nations in Latin America, the Middle East and Eastern Europe.
MODERN HISTORY - Polynesian peoples lived in New Zealand from about 700 A.D. In 1642 Dutch explorer Abel Tasman was the first European to reach New Zealand.
Sealers, whalers and traders settled here in the early 1800s and Britain established sovereignty by the Treaty of Waitangi of 1840, which guaranteed equal rights for both races.
In 1935, the first Labour (socialist) government swept to power, introducing the social welfare state and helping New Zealand's recovery from the Depression of the early 1930s.

In the 1950s and 1960s, New Zealand attained one of the highest standards of living in the world. But standards have fallen since, due largely to the oil shock of the 1970s and Britain's decision to join the European Community. ($1 = NZ$1.45)
